transcript.text: My Dyson V10 Absolute (SV12) won't run at all now. On the battery display there's a red light flashing when I press the trigger, then nothing. It was charging overnight. Do I need a new battery or is the whole thing dead?

A flashing red light followed by no power usually means the battery protection system has kicked in. This often happens if the filters are clogged (blocking airflow) or if the battery voltage has dropped too low for safety reasons. To narrow this down, please check what happens when you put it back on its charger: does a solid green light appear to show it is charging, or do the lights flash red and then go off?
On the charger the blue lights come on, then it sometimes shows the flashing red too. No green light that I've seen. The filter's clean and the bin's empty, so I don't think it's a blockage.

The fact that you see blue lights but no green charge light suggests the battery isn't accepting a full charge, likely due to a failed cell inside the pack. To confirm this, please try switching the vacuum on while it is still sitting on its charger. If it runs (even for a short time) while plugged in, the motor and electronics are fine and the battery needs replacing. If it flashes red immediately even while on the charger, the issue may be with the charger itself or the charging contacts.

I'm not sure how to test that. I haven't tried running it while it's on the charger, and I don't know if it's meant to work that way. The battery isn't swollen, hot or smelly, if that helps. It's about 4.5 years old and still the original battery.

Based on the flashing red light and the fact that it won't charge properly (no green light) after 4.5 years of use, the battery cells have likely failed internally. This is a common end-of-life issue for Dyson cordless vacuums. While the charger could theoretically be at fault, the age of the battery makes failure much more probable. If you'd like, I can help you find a compatible replacement or guide you through the removal process.

I'd rather not unscrew the battery or open anything until I've spoken to Dyson about what it would cost. Is a replacement battery the only option, or is there anything else non-invasive I should check first?

[Heading: Likely cause: battery — flat or failed (cordless)]
There are no further non-invasive checks that will fix this. The combination of a 4.5-year-old original battery, the flashing red light (indicating the protection circuit has locked out due to low voltage), and the failure to show a solid green charge light points to internal cell failure within the battery pack. Since you prefer not to open the vacuum yourself, Dyson will need to assess it; they can either replace the battery for you or advise if a repair is cost-effective given the age of the unit.
